summary: At 111 people per square mile spread across nearly 1,400 square miles of dead-flat San Joaquin Valley floor, Kings County has roughly the population density of a single suburban subdivision stretched to the horizon — and that endless geometry of irrigated farmland, dairy operations, and cotton fields is the dominant visual reality here. Agriculture and corrections anchor the economy: the Naval Air Station Lemoore, one of the Navy's premier West Coast strike fighter bases, is the single largest employer, while state prison facilities add a significant public-sector payroll, meaning job-switching without relocating is genuinely constrained to a narrow band of industries. The affordability math, however, is the headline — a median home value around $305,700 against a median household income near $68,750 yields a price-to-income ratio of roughly 4.4, strikingly accessible by California standards, though a poverty rate of 16.8% signals that this affordability reflects wage levels as much as cheap land. Summers are relentless, with average daily highs pushing well into the 80s and 90s and 9.7 hours of sunshine baking the valley haze; winters bring tule fog so thick it closes highways. Kings County is, at its core, a place where California's agricultural engine and military infrastructure meet extreme affordability and extreme climate — a combination that rewards specific professional circumstances more than casual curiosity.
